items.title: The Amazon Kindle has new AI-powered Translations
items.summary: Amazon expanded Kindle Translate (beta) to five new language pairs: English paired with Spanish, German, French, Italian and Portuguese. Self-published KDP authors can auto-translate and publish 'with a few clicks'; every translation passes an automated quality review before going live, authors can preview and set pricing, and translated titles can enroll in Kindle Unlimited. Amazon notes historically fewer than 5% of Amazon.com titles exist in more than one language. Kindle Translate launched Nov 2025 (EN<->ES, DE->EN); this is its first big language expansion.
items.notes: Single-story, product news, strongest candidate. Verified on-page date July 1, 2026.

items.title: Emaqi Looks to Grow Digital Manga Market with Subscription Service
items.summary: Emaqi, the digital manga platform from Tokyo-based Orange Inc., launched a $6.99/month premium subscription for North American English-language readers with 26,000+ volumes across ~2,500 series from major Japanese publishers (incl. Attack on Titan, upcoming Viz releases). Emaqi uses AI-assisted programs to translate, letter and produce its manga exclusives, compressing the localization pipeline. 7-day free trial plus reader incentive programs.
items.notes: Single-story. AI angle is Orange's AI-assisted translation/lettering production pipeline. Verified date July 1, 2026.

items.title: Guest Post — Now is the Time for AI in Peer Review, and Publishing Policies Need to Recognize This
items.summary: Guest post arguing that AI already has a legitimate role in scholarly peer review and that journal/publisher policies — many of which flatly ban AI in review — need updating with practical guidance instead of prohibition. Site byline date June 30, 2026.
items.notes: Single-story opinion/policy piece. Scholarly Kitchen already ran 2 cards this window (Jun 29, Jun 30 issues) — curator should weigh outlet fatigue.

items.title: Before the Guardrails: Why AI Governance in Research Must Start with Purpose
items.summary: Essay on AI governance in research publishing: argues governance frameworks should start from the purpose of scholarship rather than bolting guardrails onto tools after the fact. Site byline date June 29, 2026.
items.notes: Second Scholarly Kitchen candidate — apply <=3/outlet cap and outlet fatigue judgment; peer-review piece above is the sharper story.

items.title: In France, Publishers Confront Broad Market Challenges as Revenue Slides for a Third Consecutive Year
items.summary: French publishers' revenue fell 0.6% to EUR 2.88B in 2025 — a third straight annual decline, with over half of SNE member publishers operating at a loss. AI angle: SNE's March 2025 lawsuit against Meta over unlicensed training on French literary works heads to proceedings in early 2027, and a French bill creating a 'presumption of exploitation of cultural content by AI providers' passed the Senate unanimously but stalled in the National Assembly. Verified date June 30, 2026.
items.notes: Single-story market report; AI is a secondary but concrete thread (Meta suit, AI presumption bill). Lower priority than product/policy stories above.

items.title: Around the Book World: Monday, June 29th, 2026 — Dutch publishers launch Bookpact.ai AI-licensing platform
items.summary: ROUNDUP, but carries one otherwise-uncovered story: Dutch publishers VBK, WPG, Lannoo and Maven plus distributor CB launched Bookpact.ai, a platform letting publishers (with author consent) control and monetize AI use of their books on an opt-in, title-by-title basis — training, summarization, translation and quotation each licensed as separate use cases with separate terms, plus traceable usage reporting. No single-story coverage exists on any allowed domain (only IPA/publishersmarketplace outside the pool). Roundup's other AI items (Kobo 45% rejections, ElevenLabs Michael Caine Odyssey) are ALREADY PUBLISHED as cards — the card angle must be Bookpact only.
items.notes: Flagged roundup — prefer single-story rules apply, but Bookpact.ai is a genuinely new, distinct story unavailable elsewhere in the allowed pool. Verified date June 29, 2026.
